name: Shuffled time refused structurally
non_visual_rationale: A rule over source text whose entire output is a violations list; nothing executes, nothing renders.
criteria_delivered: 1. src/learning/declarations.ts gains rule three: RULE_HELD_OUT_STAYS_FORWARD_OF_TRAINING ('held-out-mornings-must-stay-forward-of-training'). heldOutMorningsStayForwardViolations() flags every declared `const CV_SCHEME` literal, wherever it ships, whose `kind` field is not the literal string 'rolling_origin_blocked'. Extraction (cvSchemesDeclaredIn) walks every occurrence of the marker in comment-masked text, reads the kind field out of the bracketed literal body via the same matching-bracket scan the file already used for RESIDUAL_FORMS/SIGMA_EFF, and never imports or executes what it reads (mechanism note in the file header carries over unchanged).

2. The AT's own scratch universes prove both directions: SHUFFLED_UNIVERSE (kind 'shuffled_k_fold') is refused, the violation names both the rule and the file path (join(root,'evaluation.ts')), and the cross-talk audit shows neither slice-01 rule fires on it. FORWARD_UNIVERSE (kind 'rolling_origin_blocked') is accepted -- report.violations is exactly [].

3. The shipped src/learning/cross-validation.ts (landed 05-02, CV_SCHEME.kind 'rolling_origin_blocked') needed NO change: the two pre-existing shipped-source-scanning tests (shipped-residual-inventory.test.ts 01-10, unreadable-correction-is-read-as-absent.test.ts) both assert `report.violations` deepEqual [] over the whole src/ tree and both stayed green through GREEN and the full-suite run, proving rule three does not misfire on the shipped rolling-origin declaration.

4. Slice-01's zero-violation and two-rule scenarios (tests/unit/learning-declarations.test.ts's 10 pre-existing cases, plus the two shipped-source ATs above) all stayed green UNTOUCHED -- no edit to any of them was needed. Grep confirmed slice-01 never pinned a literal 'exactly two rules' assertion anywhere in the suite (the closest text is the supersession note itself in distill/red-classification-slice-05.md); the only pins are `violations` deepEqual `[]` over universes that declare no CV_SCHEME, which stayed true by construction (absence never fires rule three).
criteria_deferred: Shape validation of CV_SCHEME beyond `kind` (e.g. malformed or missing train_weeks/test_weeks bounds) is not built -- the roadmap's stated rule is scoped exactly to kind, and no acceptance or design text asks for bounds checking. A future slice wanting that needs its own criterion.

A declared CV_SCHEME with no `kind` field at all (or an unparseable literal) is treated as `kind: null`, which the rule refuses (null !== 'rolling_origin_blocked'). This extrapolates the mined recover-branch mechanism; neither AT scenario exercises it directly, so it is documented as a design decision below rather than claimed as AT-proven.
scope_note: No conflict surfaced. The one open question going in -- whether slice-01's 'only the two named rules may produce a violation' pin would force the authorized cross-slice edit -- resolved to NO edit needed: grep across tests/ found no literal violations-count-equals-two assertion anywhere; the two tests that scan the whole shipped src/ tree assert `violations` deepEqual `[]`, which is unaffected by adding a third rule that only fires on a shape (a non-legal CV_SCHEME.kind) nothing in the shipped tree or the slice-01 fixtures declares. src/learning/cross-validation.ts (05-02, sealed a6563cf) needed no change either, exactly as the step brief anticipated.
design_decisions_not_stated_upstream: Mechanism mirrors the mined recover/learning-build:src/learning/declarations.ts rule (read read-only via `git show`, material not law) closely, adapted to this base's identical two-rule scaffold: same DeclaredCvScheme shape ({filePath, kind: string | null}), same matching-bracket body scan, same comment-masked (not string-masked) text so the quoted kind literal stays readable.

Absence of a declared CV_SCHEME anywhere in the examined universe is explicitly legal, not a violation -- cvSchemesDeclaredIn only pushes an entry when the `const CV_SCHEME` marker is actually found, so zero declarations means zero rule-three violations. Matches the roadmap's stated design intent ('the shipped source before 05-02 declared none and was legal') and is pinned by a new unit test.

A file may declare CV_SCHEME more than once; each occurrence is walked and judged independently (mirrors the mined mechanism) rather than deduplicated the way RESIDUAL_FORMS is -- CV_SCHEME is a live safety claim per declaration site, not an inventory to merge.

Chose a fast-check property test over the file's own documented default exemption ('the examination's own contract is a fixed set of syntactic shapes, not a domain invariant over a generated space') specifically for rule three: unlike the two existing rules (one fixed literal token, one specific residual form), rule three's contract genuinely generalizes over the whole space of declared kind strings, so a property (generated lowercase kind, excluding the legal value, asserting exactly one violation naming the file and the kind) adds real coverage a hardcoded string-equality bug would slip past a single example. Documented inline as a comment at the point of divergence.
acceptance: held-out-mornings-stay-forward-of-training.test.ts, pre-authored by DISTILL, describe.skip removed (the only touch made to the file). Two scenarios: (1) SHUFFLED_UNIVERSE (CV_SCHEME.kind 'shuffled_k_fold') must be refused, naming rule-three and the file path, while the cross-talk audit shows neither slice-01 rule fires; (2) FORWARD_UNIVERSE (CV_SCHEME.kind 'rolling_origin_blocked', train_weeks [1,8], test_weeks [9,10]) must be accepted with zero violations of any rule. Both scenarios pass at GREEN; no oracle was edited.
unit_law: Two tests appended to tests/unit/learning-declarations.test.ts. (1) A fast-check property, 'refuses every declared CV_SCHEME whose kind is not rolling_origin_blocked, naming the rule, the file, and the kind, for any generated kind': fc.stringMatching(/^[a-z][a-z_]{0,19}$/) filtered to exclude the legal value, numRuns 25, asserts exactly one rule-three violation per run whose detail contains both the file path and the generated kind. (2) An example test, 'accepts a universe that declares no CV_SCHEME at all: absence is legal, not a violation', pinning the design decision above.
